newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong court dismisses constitutional challenge.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong court dismisses constitutional challenge.

text.p: A Hong Kong appeals court on Tuesday crushed a challenge to the legal and constitutional arrangements that have been in place since China resumed sovereignty over the territory four weeks ago, Hong Kong cable television reported from the court.

In a ruling favouring the post-colonial government, the court dismissed a claim that pre-handover laws had ceased to be valid, and it said it had no power to rule on the legality of the provisional legislature installed by China on July 1.
The court also ruled that a criminal conspiracy case, from which the constitutional challenge arose, could continue.

Defence lawyers in the criminal case had argued that the British Common Law system used in Hong Kong had lapsed upon the handover of sovereignty and that the new legislature had failed to formally adopt pre-handover laws, creating a legal vaccuum.

It was the first constitutional challenge faced by the new China-backed government. Another challenge is expected soon when lawyers representing child illegal immigrants will argue that a new law allowing their deportation back to China is a constitutional violation.

Britain handed back its former colony to China under a 1984 Sino-British treaty allowing the territory to exercise virtual autonomy in all but defence and foreign policy, and to keep its distinct capitalist way of life intact for a further 50 years.
